dedupe_keys.name: qgis for ftth gpon network planning in poland under the european digital agenda

description: This QGIS case study describes software built in Poland to plan fibre-to-the-home (FTTH) and GPON networks so local operators could apply for European Digital Agenda co-financing. The Agenda aimed for every EU citizen to have 30 Mbps access by 2020 and at least half of them 100 Mbps; applying for funds required conceptual FTTH network maps and documentation for which no GIS tools existed. The team built wizard-style QGIS models using GRASS network algorithms, QGIS plugins (OpenLayers, QuickOSM, Scipy point clustering and their own WorkContextTracer), the QGIS modeler and SpatiaLite storage. Users load address points, cluster demand with K-means or hierarchical methods, route cables over a filtered OpenStreetMap road network using Dijkstra, place splice closures and nodes, associate nodes with addresses to estimate branch costs and export a spreadsheet report. Producer: a Polish telecom software team writing for the QGIS project; the page is dated 30 October 2016. Coverage: Poland. Access: a public web page; the tools are described as free open source but the page gives no download link or licence. Caveats: no quantitative results, scale or number of applications are reported, and the software is from 2016. Simulation uses: it is a worked example of demand clustering and least-cost cable routing for access network design and capacity planning. Related record: the Geospatial Network Inventory FTTH design tool (platform-gni-free-ftth-design).
